arguments.text: Plan (min 1): 10 km, 8 legs of 1250 m out-and-back. Start hard (shaft 265 W vs CP 200, boat 169 vs 127). Expect settle by min 2-3. If shaft power still above ~210 W after min 3, cue ease. Current helps on leg 1 (push_along +0.26), so expect opposing on even legs: judge effort by pod shaft power, not GPS pace. Target shaft power near CP (~200 W) mid-race, finish sprint last ~800-1000 m depending on pod reserve.

arguments.message: shaft power still well above CP after the start
pod reserve getting low with a long way to go
shaft power sagging well below CP

text: no cue: start phase, effort expected to settle; set watches for overpacing, low pod reserve, effort sag and the finish.

arguments.text: Settle now, ease to steady race effort, long way

Min 3.5: shaft still 233 W, pod reserve 43 pct, boat reserve 34 pct. Cued ease (no pace target, because current helps this leg ~0.3 m/s and a GPS pace would mislead after the turn). Check at next wake: want shaft near 200-205 W. If still above 215, cue ease again.

text: Cued ease: shaft power 233 W above CP 200 W with pod reserve already at 43 pct and 9.2 km to go.

arguments.text: Ease more, still too hot. Smooth long strokes, save it

Min 4.7: first ease barely took (shaft 233 to 224 W, pod reserve 34 pct). Cued ease again. Leg 2 after turn at ~1250 m is into current (~0.33 m/s), GPS pace will look slow: do not react to GPS pace, watch shaft power. Want 195-205 W.

text: Cued ease again: shaft 224 W still above CP with pod reserve 34 pct and nearly 9 km left.

arguments.text: Into current, ignore the pace. Ease back to steady

arguments.name: drag_gap
arguments.description: local push minus course-fitted push; strongly negative = extra drag (rudder snag) or blade problem

arguments.message: boat slower than shaft power and course current predict: snag on rudder or drag?

arguments.text: Min 7.7: eased to 207 W by min 6, then after turn into current rose back to 220 (chasing GPS pace). Pod reserve 21 pct, boat reserve 1 pct but no fade (-0.4) and paddler says 7/10 hard but holding: hint CP may be underestimated, not proven. Do not change CP yet; wait for cp_implied or fade evidence. Cued ease again. Added drag_gap watch (push_local minus push_along below -0.18) for rudder snag; if it fires and fade shows, consider clear_rudder.

text: Cued ease: shaft 218 W above CP into the current with pod reserve 21 pct; added a drag watch for rudder snags.

arguments.message: still above CP on a low pod reserve: re-cue with a pace target

arguments.text: Min 8.5: paddler ignoring plain ease cues (222 W, pod 14 pct, fade -2.4). Next cue: ease WITH a GPS pace target. Into current (push -0.26): CP 200 W gives water ~3.17, GPS ~2.91 = about 172 s/500. With current (+0.3) next leg: GPS ~3.45 = about 145 s/500. Added hot_recheck watch to wake me when cue gate opens.

text: no cue: cue gate closed for 23 s; set a recheck watch to re-cue ease with a pace target.

arguments.text: Reserve nearly gone. Ease now, let it recover

Min 9.0: pod reserve 11 pct, shaft 219, fade -4.7. GPS speed sliding 3.06 to 2.89 over ~60 s at constant shaft power; drag_gap drifted +0.03 to -0.12 gradually (looks like tiring blade more than a sudden rudder snag, but keep watching). Cued ease with pace 176 s/500 (into current). Next turn ~660 m ahead (about min 12.5): after turn with current, re-cue a pace near 148-150 or plain hold, else 176 is far too slow there.

arguments.condition: (heading_deg < 50 or heading_deg > 310) and elapsed_s > 660 and elapsed_s < 1000
arguments.message: turned onto leg 3 with the current: pace target 176 now too slow, re-cue

text: Cued ease with a 176 s/500 pace target: pod reserve 11 pct at 219 W, speed fading; set a watch to re-cue after the next turn.

arguments.message: cue gate open: send clear_rudder (paddler reported heavy boat, speed down at same shaft power)

arguments.text: Min 9.3: paddler says boat suddenly heavy, something on rudder? Matches data: GPS speed down ~5 pct at constant shaft ~220 W, drag_gap about -0.11. Cost of clear_rudder is a few seconds, gain if snagged is ~0.1 m/s for 8 km (about 2 min). Plan: cue clear_rudder as soon as gate opens (~min 10.2, watch gate_open_clear). Then check drag_gap recovers toward 0; if not, it was fatigue, not weed.

text: no cue: gate closed 49 s; set a watch to send clear_rudder the moment it opens (paddler and data both point to a snag).

arguments.text: Yes, likely weed. One back-stroke to clear the rudder

Min 10.2: sent clear_rudder. Before: drag_gap about -0.17 (push_local -0.44 vs push_along -0.27), speed_water 3.10, shaft 225 W, pod reserve 3.5 pct. The 176 pace target made them push harder because the snag slowed the boat. Next: confirm drag_gap back near 0 and speed up at same shaft; then cue ease (no pace) to get shaft under 200 so the pod reserve refills.

arguments.message: check whether the rudder clear worked (drag_gap, speed) and cue ease if shaft still above CP

text: Cued clear_rudder: paddler reports heavy boat and speed is down 0.17 m/s at the same shaft power; follow-up watch set.

arguments.text: Min 10.9: drag_gap sat at -0.16 then dropped to -0.52 right after the back-stroke (momentum loss, expected transient), now recovering (-0.35). Shaft climbing 222 to 256 W with pod reserve 0: paddler re-accelerating and chasing the old 176 pace. Must cue ease (no pace) at gate open (~min 11.4, after_clear_check watch). Judge snag cleared if drag_gap returns near 0 within ~40 s.

text: no cue: gate closed 25 s; drag dip is the back-stroke transient; will cue ease at gate open via the follow-up watch.

arguments.text: Rudder clear, boat is fast again. Ease right off, recover

Min 11.4: snag cleared: speed_water back to 3.30, fade back to -0.5 (was -7). But shaft 264 W with pod reserve 0 (surging after the back-stroke). Cued ease, no pace. Turn in ~250 m, then leg 3 with current. Want shaft 185-195 W for a few minutes to refill pod reserve. If paddler holds 220+ W on a 0 reserve without fading for 5+ min, CP shaft is probably underestimated: consider set_critical_power.
